title: Sell Mineral Rights in Moab, UT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Moab, UT | Cane Creek Shale
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Moab, Utah, in or around the Cane Creek shale? We buy Paradox Basin interests directly, priced against real production data.
heroLead: Moab is the county seat of Grand County and sits closest to the active Cane Creek shale development that has drawn renewed operator interest in horizontal drilling over the past decade.
intro: Moab's identity today is centered on tourism and its red-rock scenery, but the county seat also sits closest to the Cane Creek shale trend, produced through horizontal wells drilled southwest of town into the Paradox Basin's organic-rich evaporite cycles. Mineral ownership near Moab ranges from interests tied directly to active Cane Creek units to older acreage connected to the region's decades-old conventional and potash mining history.

We buy mineral and royalty interests near Moab directly. Because Cane Creek's structural complexity means value can vary meaningfully even between adjacent units, we always confirm the specific well or unit tied to your legal description before making an offer.

sections.heading: Proximity to the active Cane Creek fairway
paragraphs: Owners whose interests sit within or near the current Cane Creek horizontal development area southwest of Moab have generally seen more consistent operator interest than acreage further out, and that shows up in how we approach valuation — recent permitting and offset drilling near your specific tract carry real weight. If your interest is not yet tied to a producing well but sits near active development, that proximity is still worth discussing.

sections.heading: Layered history beyond oil and gas
paragraphs: Grand County's mineral estate near Moab also includes a long potash mining history, tied to the same evaporite geology that makes Cane Creek productive, and some older deeds in the area carry reservations or severances covering potash and other solid minerals alongside oil and gas. We check this as part of our title review, since it can affect exactly what a given interest includes.

sections.heading: Tourism growth, mineral estate unaffected
paragraphs: Moab's transformation into one of the busiest outdoor recreation destinations in the Southwest has changed the surface economy dramatically, but it has no bearing on who owns the mineral estate underneath any given tract. Whether your family's interest sits beneath a working ranch, a subdivided residential lot, or land near the national park entrances, we evaluate it purely on its production history and legal description.

faqs.question: Is my Moab-area interest inside the active Cane Creek fairway?
faqs.answer: It depends on the exact section. We confirm this against current permitting and production records before making an offer.

faqs.question: Does my deed possibly include potash rights along with oil and gas?
faqs.answer: It's possible with older Grand County deeds. We check the reservation and conveyance language as part of our title review.

faqs.question: My interest isn't producing yet but is near new development. Is it worth discussing?
faqs.answer: Yes, proximity to active drilling is a real factor we weigh even for interests without current production.

faqs.question: Does Moab's tourism growth change what my mineral interest is worth?
faqs.answer: No, surface development and tourism have no bearing on the mineral estate, which we value based on production history and legal description alone.
